items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: He had a copyist by a name of Jack Mazel, or Meizel... Jack's room was piled to the ceiling with Benny Carter arrangements... And he would go around and sell the arrangements.

ctx.x: Well, let's see, Benny Goodman was trying to have a band at Billy Rose's joint on 53rd Street there, which is now the Hammerstein Theater, and he was having a rough time. I remember I even gave him a couple of arrangements. And he and Benny Carter -- and I remember this as clearly as though it was right now. Were rather disgusted with the reception of jazz, you know, or of big band jazz particularly, and jazz in general, and we sat one time at a table there at the Park Central, plotting a European -- we were all…

But nothing ever came of it because Benny you know, managed to get going and he -- well, you know, a lot of things are talked of that never happen. But I remember talking about it. Of course every band in New York that was any kind of a band at all had a Benny Carter arrangement in the book. He wrote more arrangements that he was not paid for, because he had a copyist by the name of Jack Mazel, or Meizel, and every time Benny would make an arrangement Jack would make an extra copy for himself. Jack's room was…
Did Benny know how they were getting in all those books?
